newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Commerzbank increases stake in Morocco bank to $100 million.
newsitem.headline: Commerzbank increases stake in Morocco bank to $100 million.

text.p: German Commerzbank raised its investment to $100 million in Morocco's leading Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur,the BMCE Chairman Othman Benjelloun said on Saturday.

An agreement signing ceremony took place on Saturday at the finance ministry headquarters, attended by Commerzbank chairman Martin Kohl Hausen, King Hassan's adviser Andre Azoulay, BMCE chairman and other Moroccan senior officials.
"With the present agreement, Commerzbank raised its stake in BMCE to 10 percent from 1.6 percent or the equivalent of $100 million in terms of the current market price," Benjelloun told reporters.
Commerzbank new investment is the first biggest investment by Germany in the Moroccan private sector for decades, a Moroccan senior official said.

"Beyond the 10 percent financial stake the Commerzbank is taking in BMCE, it is a proof of confidence in Morocco's banking system and a signal that other investors should be attracted," Kohl Hausen told the ceremony.
Commerzbank has business offices in 47 countries including Morocco, Hausen added.
The signing agreement coincided with the inauguration of the first German chamber of commerce in Morocco's financial centre of Casablanca on Monday, a German banker said.
The chamber was the 75th German trade office abroad which aimed at "boosting business and exchanges between Germany and Morocco," he said.

"The Commerzbank-BMCE deal is considered as a historic event and strategic investment which underlines the German financial institution's confidence in the future of the privatised BMCE," Azoulay said.
CommerzBank held 1.6 percent holding in the Moroccan bank just after its privatisation in May, 1995, and before its latest move to increase its stake in the bank's capital.
The 8.4 percent stake newly acquired by Commerzbank was held by the state-owned Caisse de Depot et de Gestion fund in BMCE, officials said.
BMCE's capital stands at 1.44 billion dirhams divided into 14.4 million shares of 100 dirhams nominal value.
BMCE, in its recent consolidated results showed a net profits of 365.7 million dirhams ($39.7 million) in 1996 from 301 million dirhams the year before.
The results included business throughout Morocco and at the bank's Paris agency and in the Tangier free zone in northern Morocco.
Turnover in Morocco for 1996 was 2.43 billion dirhams from 2.23 billion dirhams in 1995. It gave no consolidated turnover figure.

Early 1996, it increased its capital to 1.4 billion dirhams, through incorporation of reserves, a share distribution of two new shares for seven, and a $60 million international issue of Global Depository Receipts.
The stock was last traded at 616 dirhams per share.
